subject: what if rents drop 10 percent
preheader: sensitivity analysis is the question most pros never ask.
headline: If your deal only works in the base case, it's not a deal.
body: Sensitivity analysis is the practice of asking 'what if I'm wrong?' What if rents drop 10%? What if interest rates rise another point on refinance? What if vacancy doubles? What if insurance jumps 50%?

A property generating $400/mo cash flow at $2,000 rent generates $200/mo at $1,800 rent. Cut rent another 5% (recession scenario) and you're $0. Cut expenses to keep up? Maintenance doesn't care about your spreadsheet.

Here's a real sensitivity grid I ran on a deal last month. Base case: $375/mo cash flow at $1,950 rent and 8% vacancy. If rent drops to $1,800 and vacancy goes to 12% (mild recession), cash flow becomes negative $90/mo. If insurance also jumps 20%, negative $230/mo. Same property, plausible adverse scenarios, total swing of $600/mo.

The pros run this grid before every deal. Most amateurs run a single base case and hope. A property that's cash-flow positive across a reasonable sensitivity grid is a real deal. One that only works in the base case is a bet on optimism.
